diagnosis.summary: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the 10:15 deployment, breaching the SLO. The issue is linked to the new connection pool configuration in the deployment.
diagnosis.root_cause: The migration to orders-client v3 reduced the database connection pool size and timeout settings, causing connection exhaustion and increased latency.

evidence.finding: Production p95 latency is 2150 ms, breaching the SLO of 400 ms.
Staging p95 latency is 180 ms with the same version, indicating the issue is environment-specific.
The commit a91f3c2 removed database pool settings and set max_connections to 10 and acquire_timeout_ms to 2000.
Production connection pool is fully utilized (in_use: 10, max_connections: 10) with 143 waiting connections.
Production acquire_wait_p95_ms is 1800 ms, indicating long waits for database connections.
All pods are running and healthy with the new version v4.17.
The migration to orders-client v3 is the likely cause of the connection pool configuration change.
Baseline max_connections in production was 50, but the new configuration set it to 10.

ruled_out: The staging environment with the same version does not show latency issues, ruling out a general code bug.
The deployment did not affect other services, ruling out a shared infrastructure issue.

proposal.rationale: The Checkout API's p95 latency has increased to 2150 ms in production after the deployment of version v4.17, breaching the SLO. The issue is linked to the new connection pool configuration that reduced the database connection pool size and timeout settings, causing connection exhaustion and increased latency. Rolling back to the previous version, v4.16, is the safest remediation to restore the service to its stable state.
